dedupe_keys.name: energy transition minerals and their intersection with land connected peoples owen et al 2023

description: This case study geolocates 5,097 projects for about 30 energy transition minerals and metals, such as nickel and platinum-group metals for electrolysers and fuel cells, against indicators of indigeneity, human modification of land, food production, water risk and conflict, and measures of national capacity for permitting, consultation and consent. It was written by John Owen, Deanna Kemp, Alex Lechner, Jill Harris, Ruilian Zhang and Éléonore Lèbre and published in Nature Sustainability on 1 December 2022 (volume 6, 2023), with an author correction in January 2023. Coverage is global, excluding OECD countries from part of the analysis, with mining project data from the S&P Capital IQ Pro database. The article is free under CC BY 4.0, and the dataset analysed is available in The University of Queensland repository, with source data provided with the paper. Findings: more than half of the resource base lies on or near the lands of Indigenous and peasant peoples, and China, Mexico, Peru, South Africa and Brazil have the most projects exceeding medium thresholds on both sets of measures. Caveats: project data come from a commercial database, and early-stage projects without reported resources are under-covered. For simulation it shows where social, water and conflict risks could disrupt mineral supply for energy infrastructure. It is related to the WRI global mining in socially vulnerable areas record in this catalogue. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (article); dataset under UQ eSpace general usage terms.
